pr_title: [Fix #13299] Fix `Style/BlockDelimiters` to always accept braces when an operator method argument is chained
pr_body:
Update `Style/BlockDelimiters` to not register an offense when braces are necessary to avoid changing precedence. Previously when an operator method was encountered, it was automatically evaluated (ie. not marked as ignored), but this can result in block delimiters being changed that affects block binding.

Now operator methods are evaluated for nodes to ignore, other than if it only has a single argument which is of block type.

As well, I added the missing `expect_corrections` tests for offenses without it.

Fixes #13299.

issue_context.title: Autocorrect from `Layout/LineLength` can rewrite blocks into incompatible variants
issue_context.body:
Reported in https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/discussions/13294

## Expected behavior

```yml
AllCops:
  NewCops: enable

Style/FormatString:
  Enabled: false

Style/SymbolProc:
  Enabled: false

Layout/LineLength:
  Max: 55
```

```rb
# frozen_string_literal: true

def foo(*, help:, **)
  pp help
end

foo :bar, :baaaaaaaaaaz, baaaaat: 'aaaaa',
                         help: 'Some text: %s' %
                               %w[foo bar].map { |v| v.upcase }.join(', ')
```

I expect the autocorrect to be safe.

## Actual behavior

`Layout/LineLength` triggers, rewriting the block to be multiline which somehow breaks things:

```rb
# frozen_string_literal: true

def foo(*, help:, **)
  pp help
end

foo :bar, :baaaaaaaaaaz, baaaaat: 'aaaaa',
                         help: 'Some text: %s' %
                               %w[foo bar].map do |v|
                                 v.upcase
                               end.join(', ')
# $ ruby test.rb
# "Some text: #<Enumerator:0x00007edb3df00518>"
# test.rb:11:in `<main>': undefined method `join' for an instance of String (NoMethodError)
#
#                                end.join(', ')
#                                   ^^^^^
```

Probably the ast has some different nesting levels. I am not quite sure.

## RuboCop version

```
$ [bundle exec] rubocop -V
1.66.1 (using Parser 3.3.5.0, rubocop-ast 1.32.3, running on ruby 3.3.5) [x86_64-linux]
```
comments:
Even though it might be exactly the same thing, this is also an issue when not chaining:

```ruby
...
    empty = [[nil, nil]]
...
                                                  options: empty + Arr.all.map do |t|
                                                    [t.code, t.id.to_s]
                                                  end
...

# org.jruby.exceptions.TypeError: (TypeError) no implicit conversion of Enumerator into Array
```

PS: I tried with

```yaml
Style/BlockDelimiters:
  EnforcedStyle: braces_for_chaining
```
Similar to #13096, this actually a bug in `Style/BlockDelimiters`, not `Layout/LineLength`. I opened #13544 to fix.

I'll check it against the codebase in-question also, after https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/discussions/13514 is figured out.

Those two I guess are the most critical issues "outside of one's control" (as in altering code logic, and making CI unstable) between https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/issues/stdedos and https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/discussions?discussions_q=is%3Aopen+author%3Astdedos+is%3Aunanswered+ (which are "still issues", but of a little-to-a-lot-more "fluid nature").

review_comments: The tests that were starting on lines 341 and 371 were duplicates and have been removed now that the tests higher up have `expect_correction` checks.
